core_obligations: Reduce to the case where the spectrum of A-hat is equidimensional by replacing A with A/p for a minimal prime p (proof lines 32444-32446).
Recall that it suffices to show every local ring essentially of finite type over A is catenary (proof lines 32447-32449).

Further reduce to showing that A[x_1, ..., x_n]_m is catenary for a maximal ideal m of A[x_1, ..., x_n] lying over the maximal ideal of A, using that quotients and localizations of catenary rings are catenary (proof lines 32450-32455).

Let m' be the unique maximal ideal of A-hat[x_1, ..., x_n] lying over m, and observe that the displayed map A[x_1, ..., x_n]_m -> A-hat[x_1, ..., x_n]_{m'} is local and flat because the completion map is flat (proof lines 32456-32461).

Conclude that it suffices to show the ring on the right, namely A-hat[x_1, ..., x_n]_{m'}, is catenary with equidimensional spectrum, which the formal catenarity hypothesis supplies (proof lines 32462-32463 and following).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a formally catenary Noetherian local ring A is universally catenary (source lines 32437-32441). The proof is a chain of reductions followed by a flatness argument. It first replaces A by A/p for a minimal prime p, so that the spectrum of the completion A-hat may be assumed equidimensional; then it reduces the universal catenarity assertion to showing that every local ring essentially of finite type over A is catenary, and further to showing that A[x_1, ..., x_n]_m is catenary for a maximal ideal m lying over the maximal ideal of A (proof lines 32444-32455). The substantive step introduces the unique maximal ideal m' of A-hat[x_1, ..., x_n] lying over m and uses that the displayed map A[x_1, ..., x_n]_m -> A-hat[x_1, ..., x_n]_{m'} is local and flat because completion is flat; it then observes that it suffices to prove the ring on the right is catenary with equidimensional spectrum, which is where formal catenarity enters (proof lines 32456-32463 and following). The non-routine content is the reduction to a single flat local extension of the polynomial ring and the appeal to equidimensionality of the completed spectrum.
